channel.title: The Pantry Journal
channel.description: A small, opinionated shop of countertop cooking appliances: air fryers and the thermometers that go with them. Five machines. Three guides. No invented verdicts.

item.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
item.description: The first decision is not brand or size. It is whether you want a drawer you shake or a door you open — and everything else follows from that.

item.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air-fryer capacity
item.description: The number on the box is a volume, not a portion. Here is how to turn it into something you can check against your own kitchen in five minutes.

item.title: How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs
item.description: The appliance you resent is the one that does not fit. Six questions that decide whether a machine earns a permanent place on your counter.

item.title: Chefman 6 Quart Dual Basket Air Fryer — Dual-basket air fryer
item.description: Two independent drawers, each the size of a small basket fryer. The listing is explicit about the split: 6 quarts total means 2 x 3 quarts, not one deep 6-quart basket.

item.title: Emeril Lagasse 26QT French Door Air Fryer Oven — French-door air fryer oven
item.description: An oven with French doors and an air-fry mode, sold as one appliance. The 26-quart figure is the interior, not a basket, so the comparison with a drawer fryer is not like for like.

item.title: Chefman TurboFry 8 Qt Air Fryer — Single-basket air fryer
item.description: One deep basket, 8 quarts, four named modes. This is the least complicated shape in the set, and for a lot of kitchens that is the whole argument.

item.title: ThermoMaven Instant-Read Meat Thermometer — Instant-read digital thermometer
item.description: The cheapest useful piece of kit in this set, and the one that answers a food-safety question rather than a convenience one.

item.title: CHEF iQ Sense Wireless Meat Thermometer — Wireless leave-in thermometer
item.description: A leave-in probe that talks to a phone. It answers a different question from a handheld: not what is the temperature now, but when will it be ready.
